emergency_contacts.note: 1930 is run 24/7 by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs, for reporting financial fraud specifically.

entries.rule: No bank, financial institution, or the RBI will ever ask you to share your OTP, PIN, CVV, password, or KYC documents over a phone call, SMS, or email.
entries.red_flag_context: A caller claiming to be from your bank, RBI, or a payment company asks you to read out an OTP or share a PIN to 'verify', 'unblock', or 'update' your account.
entries.source: RBI public advisory, reported via Business Standard, Aug 2024

entries.rule: The RBI does not open accounts for members of the public, take public deposits, or send emails/SMS about lottery winnings or foreign fund transfers.
entries.red_flag_context: A message claims to be from the RBI announcing a prize, lottery win, or a large sum of money awaiting transfer, and asks for a small 'processing fee' first.
entries.source: RBI public advisory, reported via Business Standard, Aug 2024

entries.rule: You never need to enter your UPI PIN to RECEIVE money. Entering a PIN is only required to send/pay money.
entries.red_flag_context: Someone posing as a buyer on an online marketplace sends a 'collect request' via UPI and asks you to enter your PIN to 'accept' a payment.
entries.source: Punjab & Sind Bank cyber fraud awareness page, citing RBI guidance

entries.rule: Legitimate part-time job or investment offers do not require you to 'load money' into a platform before you can withdraw earnings, and do not route payments through unauthorized third-party UPI IDs.
entries.red_flag_context: A job or investment offer over WhatsApp/Telegram asks you to complete small paid 'tasks' and deposit money to unlock larger returns.
entries.source: RBI Advisory on Frauds/Cybercrimes through investment and part-time job scams, via Federal Bank

entries.rule: Financial cyber fraud in India should be reported immediately via the 1930 helpline or cybercrime.gov.in — the faster it's reported, the higher the chance of freezing the funds before they're withdrawn.
entries.red_flag_context: Used as the standard 'next step' recommendation any time the check-in verdict concludes a scam is likely, or already happened.
entries.source: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal / I4C, Ministry of Home Affairs

universal_fallback_patterns.note: Used for any country_code without a populated dictionary yet. Jurisdiction-agnostic, safe to show anywhere.
patterns: No legitimate institution asks for your password, PIN, OTP, or full card number over phone, SMS, or email — ever, under any pretext.
Urgency plus secrecy together is the core scam pattern: 'act now' combined with 'don't tell anyone' is designed to stop you from checking with someone you trust.
If in doubt, hang up and call back using a number from your card, bank statement, or the institution's official website — never a number the caller gave you.
Nobody legitimate asks you to pay a fee upfront to receive a prize, lottery win, or inheritance.
